paragraphs: We believe Southern Copper Corporation ("SCC", "Southern Copper" or the "Company") is one of the largest integrated copper producers in the world. Our major production includes copper, molybdenum, zinc and silver. All of our mining, smelting and refining facilities are located in Peru and Mexico, and we conduct exploration activities in those countries and in Argentina and Chile. See Item 2 "Properties—Review of Operations" for maps of our principal mines, smelting facilities and refineries. The considerable scale of our operations makes us one of the largest mining companies in Peru and Mexico. We believe we have the largest copper reserves in the world. We were incorporated in Delaware in 1952 and have conducted copper mining operations since 1960. Since 1996, our common stock has been listed on both the New York and Lima Stock Exchanges.

Our Peruvian copper operations involve mining, milling and flotation of copper ore to produce copper; the smelting of copper concentrates to produce blister and anode copper; and the refining of anode copper to produce copper cathodes. As part of this production process, we also produce significant amounts of molybdenum concentrate and sulfuric acid. Our precious metals plant at the Ilo refinery produces refined silver, gold, and other materials. Additionally, we produce refined copper using solvent extraction/electrowinning technology ("SX-EW"). We operate the Toquepala and Cuajone open-pit mines high in the Andes Mountains, approximately 860 kilometers southeast of the city of Lima, Peru. We also operate a smelter and refinery west of the Toquepala and Cuajone mines in the coastal city of Ilo, Peru.

Our Mexican operations are conducted through our subsidiary, Minera Mexico, S.A. de C.V. ("Minera Mexico"), which we acquired in 2005. Minera Mexico engages primarily in the mining and processing of copper, molybdenum, zinc, silver, gold and lead. Minera Mexico operates through subsidiaries that are grouped into three separate units. Mexicana de Cobre, S.A. de C.V. (together with its subsidiaries, the "La Caridad" unit) operates La Caridad, an open-pit copper mine, the Pilares open-pit copper mine, a copper ore concentrator, a SX-EW plant, a smelter, refinery and a rod plant. The La Caridad refinery has a precious metals plant that produces refined silver, gold and other materials. Operadora de Minas e Instalaciones Mineras, S.A de C.V. (the "Buenavista unit") operates Buenavista, an open-pit copper mine, which is located on the site of one of the world's largest copper ore deposits, two copper concentrators, a zinc concentrator and two operating SX-EW plants. Industrial Minera Mexico, S.A. de C.V. (together with its subsidiaries, the "IMMSA unit") operates five underground mines that produce zinc, lead, copper, silver and gold, and a zinc refinery.

We utilize modern, state of the art mining and processing methods, including global positioning systems and computerized mining processes. Our operations have a high level of vertical integration, which allows us to use our facilities, employees and equipment to manage the entire production process, including ore mining and production of refined copper rod and other products, and to execute most associated transport and logistics functions.

The sales prices for our products are largely determined by market forces beyond our control. Our management, therefore, focuses on cost control and production enhancement to remain profitable. We endeavor to achieve these goals through capital spending programs, exploration efforts and cost reduction programs. Our focus is on remaining profitable during periods of low copper prices and maximizing results in periods of high copper prices. For additional information on the sale prices of the metals we produce, please see "Metal Prices" in this Item 1.

Unless stated otherwise, all our financial information is presented in U.S. dollars and any reference herein to "U.S. dollars," "dollars," or "$" are to U.S. dollars; references to "sol," "soles" or "S/", signify Peruvian soles; and references to "peso," "pesos," or "Ps.," represent Mexican pesos.

Unless otherwise noted, all tonnages are in metric tonnes. To convert to short tons, multiply by 1.102. All ounces are troy ounces. All distances are in kilometers. To convert to miles, multiply by 0.621. To convert hectares to acres, multiply by 2.47.

The following chart describes our organizational structure, starting with our controlling stockholders, as of December 31, 2025. For the purpose of clarity, the chart identifies only our main subsidiaries and eliminates intermediate holding companies.

We are a majority-owned, indirect subsidiary of Grupo Mexico S.A.B. de C.V. ("Grupo Mexico"). As of December 31, 2025, Grupo Mexico, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Americas Mining Corporation ("AMC"), owned 88.9% of our capital stock. Grupo Mexico's principal business is to act as a holding company for the shares of other corporations engaged in the mining, processing, purchase and sale of minerals and other products and in the provision of railway and other related services.

We conduct our operations in Peru through a registered branch (the "SPCC Peru Branch," "Branch" or "Peruvian Branch"). The SPCC Peru Branch comprises virtually all of our assets and liabilities associated with our copper operations in Peru. The SPCC Peru Branch does not constitute a corporation that is separate from SCC, and, as such, the obligations of the SPCC Peru Branch are direct obligations of SCC and vice-versa. The SPCC Peru Branch is, however, registered as a branch of a foreign company pursuant to Peruvian law and through this entity, we hold assets, incur liabilities and conduct operations in Peru. Although the SPCC Peru Branch has no capital or liability that is separate from that held or applicable to SCC, the SPCC Peru Branch is deemed to have equity capital for purposes of determining the economic interests of holders of our investment shares (See Note 14 "Stockholders' Equity" of the consolidated financial statements).

In April 2005, we acquired Minera Mexico, from Americas Mining Corporation ("AMC"), a subsidiary of Grupo Mexico, our controlling stockholder. Minera Mexico is a holding company and all of its operations are conducted through subsidiaries that are grouped into three units: (i) the La Caridad unit, (ii) the Buenavista unit and (iii) the IMMSA unit. We own 99.998% of Minera Mexico.

In 2008, our Board of Directors authorized a $500 million share repurchase program that has since been increased by the Board of Directors and is currently authorized for up to $3 billion. No repurchases have been made under this program since the third quarter of 2016. Through December 31, 2025, we have repurchased an aggregate of 119.5 million shares of our common stock for an aggregate cost of $2.9 billion. These repurchased shares may be used for general corporate purposes. We may purchase additional shares under the program from time to time, based on market conditions and other factors. This repurchase program does not have an expiration date and may be modified or discontinued at any time. Since the second quarter of 2024, the Board of Directors has approved quarterly stock dividends, and a portion of these repurchased shares have been used to pay these dividends to our common stockholders.

Our revenues are derived primarily from our operations in Peru and Mexico. Risks related to our operations in both countries include those associated with economic and political conditions, the effects of currency fluctuations and inflation, the effects of government regulations and the geographic concentration of our operations.

Copper is an important component in the world's infrastructure chain. It is the third most widely used metal, after iron and aluminum. Copper has unique chemical and physical properties, including high ductility; malleability; thermal and electrical conductivity; and resistance to corrosion, and as such, is considered a prime material for use in electrical and electronic products, including components for power transmission and generation, which accounts for about three quarters of copper global use, and for telecommunications, building construction, transportation and industrial machinery. Copper is also an important metal in non-electrical applications such as plumbing and roofing and, when alloyed with zinc to form brass, is used in many industrial and consumer applications.

headings: Financial risks
Our financial performance is highly dependent on the price of copper and the other metals we produce.
Volatility in metals prices may also impact the price of our outstanding securities.
Our business requires levels of capital investments that we may not be able to maintain.
Restrictive covenants in the agreements governing our indebtedness and the indebtedness of our Minera Mexico subsidiary may restrict our ability to pursue our business strategies.
We may not pay a significant amount of our net income as cash dividends on our common stock in the future.
Our ability to recognize the benefits of deferred tax assets is dependent on future cash flows and taxable income.
Operational risks
Our actual reserves and resources may not conform to our current estimates of our ore deposits and our long-term viability depends on our ability to replenish mineral reserves and resources.
Our operations are subject to risks, some of which are not insurable.
Changes in the demand level for our products and copper sales agreements could adversely affect our revenues.

Interruptions of energy supply or increases in energy, fuel and gas costs, shortages of water supply, critical parts, equipment, skilled labor and other production costs may adversely affect our results of operations.

Our Company is subject to health and safety laws that may restrict our operations, result in operational delays or increase our operating costs and adversely affect our financial results of operations.
Our metals exploration efforts are highly speculative in nature and may be unsuccessful.
We may be adversely affected by challenges relating to slope stability.
We may be adversely affected by labor disputes.
Our mining operations or metal production projects may be subject to stoppage and additional costs due to community actions and other factors.
Environmental regulation, climate change and other regulations may increase our costs of doing business, restrict our operations or result in operational delays.
Our mining and metal production projects may expose us to new risks.
Our business depends upon information technology systems that may be adversely affected by disruptions, damage, cyber-attacks, failure and risks associated with implementation and integration.
Our business is exposed to certain risks associated with artificial intelligence ("AI") and other new technologies.
Global and local market conditions, including the high competitiveness in the copper mining industry, may adversely affect our profitability.
We are controlled by Grupo Mexico, which exercises control over our affairs and policies and whose interests may be different from yours.
Unanticipated litigation or negative developments in pending litigation or with respect to other contingencies may adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Developments in the United States, Europe and emerging market countries may adversely affect the Company business, the market value and trading price of our common stock and our debt securities.
Potential developments in U.S. policy, regulatory uncertainty, threats or imposition of tariffs and trade tensions may materially affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Other international risks
Risks Associated with Doing Business in Peru and Mexico
There is uncertainty as to the termination and renewal of our mining concessions.
Peruvian economic and political conditions, as well as illegal mining activities may have an adverse impact on our business.
Mexican economic and political conditions, as well as drug-related violence, may have an adverse impact on our business.
Peruvian inflation and fluctuations in the sol exchange rate may adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Mexican inflation, restrictive exchange control policies and fluctuations in the peso exchange rate may adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
paragraphs: Every investor or potential investor in Southern Copper Corporation should carefully consider the following risk factors.

Our financial performance is significantly affected by the market prices of the metals that we produce, particularly the market prices of copper, molybdenum, zinc and silver. Historically, these prices have been subject to wide fluctuations and are affected by numerous and complex factors beyond our control. Market prices are affected by a number of factors, including global economic and political conditions in general, and in particular by: international policies and regulations in the ambits of trade, taxes and tariffs; levels of supply and demand; the availability and cost of substitutes; inventory levels maintained by users; actions of participants in the commodities markets; interest rates; expectations regarding future inflation rates; currency exchange rates and changes in technology. In addition, the market prices of copper and certain other metals have on occasion been subject to rapid short-term changes. At the start of the pandemic in 2020, copper prices were initially negatively impacted by economic uncertainty. Copper prices began to recover in mid-2020 and continued to strengthen, reaching record levels in 2025. Volatility in global economic growth, particularly in developing countries, has the potential to adversely affect future demand and prices for commodities. Geopolitical uncertainty and protectionism have the potential to inhibit international trade and negatively impact business confidence, which can create price volatility and constraints on our ability to trade in certain markets.
In addition to the factors discussed above, copper prices may be affected by demand from China, which is currently the largest consumer of refined copper and concentrate in the world.

Over the last three years, approximately 75.9% of our revenues were generated from the sale of copper; 10.9% from molybdenum; 5.7% from silver; and 3.6% from zinc. Please see the distribution of our revenues per product on Item 8 "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" Note 18 "Segment and Related Information—Sales value per segment".
See also the historical average price of our products on Item 1 Business caption "Metals prices".

We cannot predict if metals prices will rise or fall in the future. Extended significant future declines in metals prices, particularly copper, could have a material adverse impact on our results of operations, financial condition and value of our assets. Under very adverse market conditions, we might consider curtailing or modifying some of our mining and processing operations. We may be unable to decrease our costs in an amount sufficient to offset reductions in revenues, in which case, we may incur losses, which may be material.

paragraphs: This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations relates to and should be read together with our Audited Consolidated Financial Statements as of and for each of the years in the three-year period ended December 31, 2025. Therefore, unless otherwise noted, the discussion below of our financial condition and results of operations is for Southern Copper Corporation and its subsidiaries (collectively, "SCC," "Southern Copper," "the Company," "our," and "we") on a consolidated basis for all periods. Our financial results may not be indicative of our future results.

This discussion contains forward-looking statements that are based on management's current expectations, estimates and projections about our business and operations. Our actual results may differ materially from those currently anticipated and expressed in the forward-looking statements as a result of a number of factors. See Item 1 "Business—Cautionary Statement."
For details on the discussion on variations between 2024 and 2023, please see Management´s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, on the 2024 Form 10-K.

Business: Our business is primarily the production and sale of copper. In the process of producing copper, a number of valuable metallurgical by-products are recovered, which we also produce and sell. Market forces outside of our control largely determine the sale prices for our products. Our management, therefore, focuses on value creation through copper production, cost control, production enhancement and maintaining a prudent capital structure to remain profitable. We endeavor to achieve these goals through capital spending programs, exploration efforts and cost reduction programs. Our aim is to remain profitable during periods of low copper prices and to maximize financial performance in periods of high copper prices. We are one of the world's largest copper mining companies in terms of production and sales and our principal operations are in Peru and Mexico. We also have an active ongoing exploration program in Chile and Argentina.

We believe we hold one of the world's largest copper reserves and resources positions. As of December 31, 2025, our copper mineral reserves, estimated at a copper price of $3.30 per pound, totaled 108,955 million pounds of contained copper, distributed in the following locations:
Mexican open‑pit 44,154 Peruvian operations 45,527 Development projects 19,274 Total 108,955
Outlook: Various key factors affect our outcome. These include, but are not limited to, the following:

● Sales structure: In the last three years, approximately 75.9% of our revenues came from the sale of copper; 10.9% from molybdenum; 5.7% from silver; 3.6% from zinc; and 3.9% from various other products, including gold, sulfuric acid and other materials.

● Copper: In 2025, copper accounted for approximately 74.8% of our sales. The average LME copper price increased from $4.15 per pound in 2024 to $4.51 in 2025 (+8.7%), while COMEX prices rose from $4.22 to $4.82 per pound (+14.2%) in the same period.

Based on current supply and demand dynamics, we are currently estimating a copper market deficit of 320,000 tonnes for 2026. Copper inventories worldwide were at the end of January 2026 at 1,054,000 tonnes. We estimate that this inventory currently covers approximately 14 days of global demand.

● Molybdenum: Represented approximately 10.5% of our sales in 2025. Average molybdenum prices increased from $21.21 per pound in 2024 to $22.01 per pound in 2025 (+3.8%), reflecting favorable market conditions during the year.

● Silver: Silver represented 7.3% of our sales in 2025. Average silver prices increased from $28.25 per ounce in 2024 to $39.99 per pound in 2025 (+41.6%). We believe that long-term silver prices will be supported by the intensive industrial use of this metal.
● Zinc: Average zinc prices increased 3.2% in 2025 versus the figure recorded in 2024. This metal represented 3.9% of our sales in 2025.
● Production: In 2026, we expect our copper production to stand at 911,400 tonnes, mainly due to lower ore grades. We are reviewing this forecast to improve it throughout the year.

paragraphs: 我們認為 Southern Copper Corporation ("SCC", "Southern Copper" 或 the "Company") 是全球最大的整合式銅生產商之一。我們的主要生產包括銅、鉬、鋅和銀。我們所有的採礦、熔煉和提煉設施均位於祕魯和墨西哥，我們在這些國家以及阿根廷和智利進行探礦活動。請參閱第 2 項 "財產—業務回顧" 中的圖表，以瞭解我們主要礦場、熔煉設施和提煉廠的分佈。我們的業務規模龐大，使我們成為祕魯和墨西哥最大的礦業公司之一。我們認為我們擁有全球最大的銅儲備。我們於 1952 年在特拉華州註冊成立，並自 1960 年起從事銅礦開採業務。自 1996 年起，我們的普通股已在紐約證券交易所和利馬證券交易所上市交易。

我們在祕魯的銅業務涉及銅礦石的採礦、選礦和浮選，以生產銅；將銅 concentrates 熔煉以生產 blister 銅和陽極銅；以及將陽極銅提煉以生產銅陰極。作為此生產過程的一部分，我們也生產大量鉬 concentrates 和硫酸。我們在 Ilo 提煉廠的貴金屬廠生產精煉銀、金和其他材料。此外，我們使用溶劑萃取/電積法 ("SX-EW") 生產精煉銅。我們經營位於祕魯利馬東南約 860 公里的安第斯山脈高處的 Toquepala 和 Cuajone 開採坑礦。我們也在祕魯海岸城市 Ilo 的 Toquepala 和 Cuajone 礦山西側經營一座熔煉廠和提煉廠。

我們在墨西哥的業務透過我們的子公司 Minera Mexico, S.A. de C.V. ("Minera Mexico") 進行，我們於 2005 年取得該子公司。Minera Mexico 主要從事銅、鉬、鋅、銀、金和鉛的採礦和加工。Minera Mexico 透過子公司分為三個獨立單位運作。Mexicana de Cobre, S.A. de C.V.（連同其子公司，稱為 "La Caridad" 單位）運作 La Caridad 開採坑銅礦、Pilares 開採坑銅礦、銅礦石濃縮廠、SX-EW 廠、熔煉廠、提煉廠和棒材廠。La Caridad 提煉廠設有貴金屬廠，生產精煉銀、金和其他材料。Operadora de Minas e Instalaciones Mineras, S.A. de C.V.（稱為 "Buenavista" 單位）運作 Buenavista 開採坑銅礦，該礦位於全球最大銅礦石儲備之一的場地，並擁有兩座銅濃縮廠、一座鋅濃縮廠和兩座運作中的 SX-EW 廠。Industrial Minera Mexico, S.A. de C.V.（連同其子公司，稱為 "IMMSA" 單位）運作五座地下礦，生產鋅、鉛、銅、銀和金，並有一座鋅提煉廠。
我們使用現代、最先進的採礦和加工方法，包括全球定位系統和電腦化採礦程序。我們的業務具有高度的垂直整合，使我們能利用設施、員工和設備管理整個生產過程，包括礦石採礦和精煉銅棒及其他產品的生產，並執行大部分相關的運輸和物流功能。
我們產品的銷售價格主要由市場力量決定，而我們的管理層因此專注於成本控制和生產提升，以維持利潤。我們透過資本支出計劃、探礦努力和成本削減計劃來實現這些目標。我們的重點是在銅價低的時候保持利潤，在銅價高的時候最大化結果。如需有關我們生產金屬銷售價格的更多資訊，請參閱本項目第 1 項中的 "金屬價格"。
除非另有說明，我們所有的財務資訊均以美金為單位，本文中任何提及 "美金"、"美元" 或 "$" 均指美金；提及 "索爾"、"索爾" 或 "S/" 則指祕魯索爾；提及 "比索"、"比索" 或 "Ps." 則指墨西哥比索。
除非另有說明，所有產量均以公噸為單位。要轉換為短噸，請乘以 1.102。所有盎司均為英制盎司。所有距離均以公里為單位。要轉換為英里，請乘以 0.621。要轉換公頃為英畝，請乘以 2.47。
下圖說明我們的組織架構，從我們的控股股東開始，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。為明確起見，圖表僅標示我們的主要子公司，並省略中間控股公司。

本公司為Grupo Mexico S.A.B. de C.V. ("Grupo Mexico") 的多數股東間接子公司。截至2025年12月31日，Grupo Mexico 透過其全資子公司Americas Mining Corporation ("AMC") 持有本公司資本股票的88.9%。Grupo Mexico 的主要業務為擔任其他從事礦業、加工、買賣礦物及其他產品，以及提供鐵路及其他相關服務公司的持股公司。

本公司在祕魯透過註冊分支 ("SPCC祕魯分支"、"分支"或"祕魯分支") 進行營運。SPCC祕魯分支幾乎涵蓋本公司在祕魯銅礦業務的所有資產與負債。SPCC祕魯分支並非與SCC 獨立的公司，因此SPCC祕魯分支的義務為SCC 的直接義務，反之亦然。然而，SPCC祕魯分支根據祕魯法律註冊為外國公司的分支，透過此機構，本公司在祕魯持有資產、產生負債並進行營運。雖然SPCC祕魯分支並無與SCC 所持有或適用的資產或負債獨立的資本或負債，但為計算投資股份持有人的經濟權益，SPCC祕魯分支被視為具有權益資本 (請參閱財務報表附註14 "股東權益")。

2005年4月，本公司自Americas Mining Corporation ("AMC")，即本公司控股股東Grupo Mexico 的子公司，取得Minera Mexico。Minera Mexico 為一控股公司，其所有營運均透過子公司進行，這些子公司分為三個單位：(i) La Caridad 單位、(ii) Buenavista 單位及(iii) IMMSA 單位。本公司持有Minera Mexico 的99.998%。

2008年，本公司董事會核准了一項價值5億美元的股票回購計畫，此計畫隨後經董事會增加核准，目前核准總金額為30億美元。自2016年第三季以來，本公司尚未在該計畫下進行任何股票回購。截至2025年12月31日，本公司已回購總計1.195億股本公司普通股，總計成本為29億美元。這些回購股票可用於一般企業用途。本公司可能根據市場條件及其他因素，不時在該計畫下購買更多股票。此回購計畫無到期日，並可隨時修改或終止。自2024年第二季起，董事會已核准每季發放股票紅利，且部分回購股票已用於支付給本公司普通股股東的紅利。
本公司營業收入主要來自在祕魯與墨西哥的營運。與本公司在這兩個國家營運相關的風險包括經濟與政治條件、貨幣兌換率與通貨膨脹的影響、政府規範的影響，以及營運地點的地理集中性。
銅是世界基礎建設鏈中重要的零組件。它是除鐵與鋁之外使用最廣泛的金屬。銅具有獨特的化學與物理特性，包括高延展性、可塑性、熱電導性，以及抗腐蝕性，因此被視為電氣與電子產品的首選材料，包括用於電力傳輸與發電的零組件，這佔全球銅使用量的大約四分之三，以及用於電信、建築建設、運輸與工業機械。銅也是非電氣應用中的重要金屬，例如水管與屋頂工程，當銅與鋅合金形成黃銅時，則廣泛應用於許多工業與消費性產品。

paragraphs: 本項管理層討論與分析（Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations）與我們經審計之合併財務報表有關，該報表為截至2025年12月31日之三年期間內各年度之財務狀況與營運結果。因此，除非另有說明，以下對我們財務狀況與營運結果之討論係針對Southern Copper Corporation及其子公司（合稱為"SCC"、"Southern Copper"、"the Company"、"our"及"we"）於所有期間之合併財務狀況。我們之財務結果可能無法反映我們未來之財務結果。
本項討論包含前瞻性陳述，這些陳述係基於管理層目前對我們業務與營運之預期、估計與預測。我們實際之結果可能與目前預期及表達於前瞻性陳述中之結果有重大差異，原因係因多種因素所致。請參閱第1項"業務—警示聲明"。
如需有關2024年與2023年之間變動之詳細說明，請參閱2024年Form 10-K之管理層討論與分析（Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations）。

業務：我們之業務主要為銅之生產與銷售。在生產銅的過程中，會回收若干具有價值之冶金副產品，我們亦生產與銷售這些副產品。我們產品之銷售價格主要由我們無法控制之市場因素所決定。因此，我們管理層專注於透過銅之生產、成本控制、生產提升及維持謹慎之資本結構來創造價值，以維持獲利。我們致力於透過資本支出計畫、探勘努力及成本降低計畫來達成這些目標。我們之目標為在銅價低之期間維持獲利，並在銅價高之期間最大化財務表現。我們為全球最大的銅礦企業之一，以生產與銷售為準，我們之主要營運為位於祕魯與墨西哥。我們亦在智利與阿根廷進行積極之持續探勘計畫。
我們相信我們擁有全球最大的銅儲備與資源地位。截至2025年12月31日，以每磅3.30美元之銅價計算，我們之銅礦儲備總計為108,955百萬磅之銅含量，分佈於以下地點：
墨西哥露天開採 44,154 瘞魯運營 45,527 開發項目 19,274 總計 108,955
展望：多種關鍵因素影響我們之結果。這些因素包括但不限於以下：
● 売出結構：在過去三年中，我們約75.9%之營業收入來自銅之銷售；10.9%來自鉬；5.7%來自銀；3.6%來自鋅；以及3.9%來自各種其他產品，包括黃金、硫酸與其他材料。
● 銅：2025 年，銅佔我們銷售額約 74.8%。LME 銅價格平均從 2024 年每磅 4.15 美元增至 2025 年每磅 4.51 美元（+8.7%），而 COMEX 價格則從 2024 年每磅 4.22 美元增至 2025 年每磅 4.82 美元（+14.2%）。
根據目前供應與需求動態，我們目前預估 2026 年銅市場將出現 320,000 公噸的缺口。截至 2026 年 1 月底，全球銅存貨為 1,054,000 公噸。我們預估，目前存貨約可覆蓋全球需求的 14 天。
● 鎂：2025 年，鎂佔我們銷售額約 10.5%。鎂價格平均從 2024 年每磅 21.21 美元增至 2025 年每磅 22.01 美元（+3.8%），反映當年市場條件較為有利。
● 銀：2025 年，銀佔我們銷售額 7.3%。銀價格平均從 2024 年每盎司 28.25 美元增至 2025 年每磅 39.99 美元（+41.6%）。我們認為，銀的長期價格將受到該金屬廣泛工業用途的支持。
● 鋅：2025 年，鋅價格較 2024 年上升 3.2%。該金屬在 2025 年佔我們銷售額 3.9%。
● 生產：2026 年，我們預期銅產量為 911,400 公噸，主要由於礦石品位較低。我們正在審視此預測，以全年內改善其準確性。

headings: 財務風險
本公司財務表現高度依賴所生產銅及其他金屬的價格。
金屬價格波動也可能影響本公司發行在外證券的價格。
本公司業務需要一定程度的資本投資，而我們可能無法維持此投資水平。
本公司及Minera Mexico子公司債務契約中的限制性條款可能限制我們執行業務策略的能力。
本公司未來可能無法以現金股息形式支付重大部分的淨收入作為普通股股息。
本公司認列遞延所得稅資產效益的能力取決於未來現金流量及應稅所得。
營運風險
本公司實際之儲備與資源可能與目前對礦脈儲備之估計不一致，且本公司長期之可行性取決於本公司補充礦物儲備與資源之能力。
本公司之營運面臨風險，部分風險可能無法投保。
本公司產品之需求程度與銅銷售協議之變動可能對本公司營業收入造成不利影響。
能源供應中斷或能源、燃料與氣體成本之增加、水資源短缺、關鍵零組件、設備、技術人員與其他生產成本之不足，可能對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司須遵守健康與安全法規，此等法規可能限制本公司營運、導致營運延誤或增加營運成本，並對本公司財務營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司之金屬探勘工作性質極具風險，且可能無法成功。
本公司可能因斜坡穩定性之挑戰而受到不利影響。
本公司可能因勞資爭議而受到不利影響。
本公司之採礦業務或金屬生產專案可能因社區行動及其他因素而遭停工並產生額外成本。
環境法規、氣候變遷及其他法規可能提高本公司營運成本、限制本公司營運或導致營運延誤。
本公司之採礦及金屬生產專案可能使本公司面臨新風險。
本公司營運依賴資訊科技系統，該系統可能因中斷、損壞、網路攻擊、實施及整合相關風險而受到不利影響。
本公司營運面臨與人工智慧（"AI"）及其他新技術相關之特定風險。
全球及地方市場情勢，包括銅礦業高度競爭性，可能對本公司獲利能力產生不利影響。
本公司受Grupo Mexico控制，該公司控制本公司業務及政策，且其利益可能與您不同。
未預期之訴訟或現有訴訟及其他事項之不利發展可能對本公司財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
美國、歐洲及新興市場國家的發展可能對本公司業務、我們普通股的市場價值及交易價格，以及我們的債務證券產生不利影響。
美國政策的潛在變化、法規不確定性、威脅或課徵關稅及貿易緊張關係，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大影響。
其他國際風險
在祕魯及墨西哥從事業務的相關風險
我們礦業採許證的終止及續約存在不確定性。
祕魯的經濟與政治情況，以及非法採礦活動，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
墨西哥的經濟與政治情況，以及與毒品相關的暴力活動，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
祕魯的通貨膨脹及索爾匯率波動，可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
墨西哥通貨膨脹、嚴格的外匯管制政策以及比索匯率波動可能不利於本公司財務狀況及營運成果。
paragraphs: 每一個投資人或潛在投資人於 Southern Copper Corporation 應該謹慎考慮下列風險因素。

我們的財務表現受到我們所生產金屬市場價格的重大影響，特別是銅、鎂、鋅與銀的市場價格。歷史來看，這些價格曾出現大幅波動，且受到許多超出我們控制範圍的複雜因素影響。市場價格受到多種因素影響，包括總體經濟與政治條件，特別是：國際貿易、稅收與關稅政策；供給與需求水平；替代品的可得性與成本；用戶所維持的存貨水平；商品市場參與者的行動；利率；對未來通貨膨脹率的預期；貨幣兌換率以及技術的變化。此外，銅與某些其他金屬的市場價格有時會出現快速的短期波動。在 2020 年疫情初期，銅價因經濟不確定性而受到負面影響。銅價於 2020 年中開始復甦，並持續強化，於 2025 年達到歷史新高。全球經濟成長的波動，特別是在開發中國家，可能對未來商品需求與價格產生不利影響。地緣政治不確定性與保護主義可能抑制國際貿易，並對企業信心產生負面影響，這可能會造成價格波動，並限制我們在某些市場進行交易的能力。
除了上述因素外，銅價可能受到中國需求的影響，中國目前是全球最大的精銅與 concentrates 消費國。
過去三年，約 75.9% 的我們營業收入來自銅的銷售；10.9% 來自鎂；5.7% 來自銀；以及 3.6% 來自鋅。請參閱第 8 項 "財務資料與補充資料" 的註 18 "應報告分部與相關資訊—各分部銷售價值"，以瞭解我們收入的產品分佈。
請參閱第 1 項 "業務" 的 "金屬價格" 部分，以瞭解我們產品的歷史平均價格。
我們無法預測未來金屬價格將上漲或下跌。未來金屬價格，特別是銅價，若出現長時間顯著下跌，可能對我們的營運成果、財務狀況與資產價值產生重大不利影響。在非常惡劣的市場條件下，我們可能會考慮削減或修改部分礦業與處理作業。我們可能無法減少足夠的成本以彌補收入減少，因此，我們可能會產生虧損，這可能具有重大影響。
